parsed.summary: The Lean theorem says the following. Take a wave amplitude `a` in the wave class W_α, with weight √ζ·P. Assume the phase normal of the field (V_r, V_θ, V_z, Φ) has polynomial jet bounds and satisfies 0 < b ≤ |n_Φ| ≤ M on the strip domain. Assume V_r ∈ M_{-κ}, V_θ ∈ M_0, V_z ∈ M_1 and 1/R ∈ M_0 (all unweighted), and 1/K_n = O(ε_n^{1/2}·slow^p). Then the curl remainder of the curl-generated coefficient lies in W_{α+1/2-κ}. The quoted paper Lemma 9.2 is a different result, so the declaration appears mispaired with the excerpt. The paper lemma concerns mean–wave and wave–wave transport products (w·∇*)v + (v·∇*)w, with exponent α+μ−1/2. The Lean result is about a curl remainder with exponent α+1/2−κ. The key caveat is that the core objects (`curlRemainder`, `coefficient`, `phaseNormal`, `MemClass`, `StripData`) are not visible, so faithfulness even to the candidate-manuscript lemma cannot be checked here.

glossary.plain: A band-indexed scalar sequence a_n satisfies |a_n| ≤ C·ε_n^β·slow_n^p for some C ≥ 0 and some p ∈ ℕ.
glossary.standard_concept: Band-uniform size bound of order ε^β up to polynomial slow factors
glossary.note: The meaning of s.epsilon and s.slow is not visible.

glossary.plain: Each f_i is C^∞ on its chart. For every N, all derivatives up to order N are bounded by C·scale_i^m, uniformly in i.
Membership in MemClass with weight 1 and exponent α (a mean class M_α).
Membership in MemClass with weight √ζ(x)·P_n(x) and exponent α.
glossary.note: MemClass is not shown. Real.sqrt of a negative ζ would give 0.
In the theorem it is shadowed by the bound variable {M : ℝ}, so it is irrelevant to the statement.
In the theorem, `a` is used as an ℕ → D → E sequence satisfying WaveClass. It is presumably an auto-bound variable, not this def.

lean_claims.plain: Hypotheses: the phase normals n_Φ^(n) have uniform polynomial jets on the phase domain; a ∈ W_α (weight √ζ·P); b > 0 and b ≤ |n_Φ^(n)(x)| ≤ M for x in s.domain; κ ≥ 0; V_r ∈ M_{-κ}, V_θ ∈ M_0, V_z ∈ M_1, 1/R ∈ M_0; and |1/K_n| ≤ C·ε_n^{1/2}·slow_n^p. Conclusion: n ↦ curlRemainder(K_n, R, V^(n), coefficient(R, V^(n), Φ_n, a_n)) belongs to W_{α+1/2−κ} with the same weight √ζ·P.

paper_claims.plain: If w ∈ W_α is a wave and v is a mean field with tangential components in M_μ and radial component in M_{μ+1}, then the nonzero harmonics of (w·∇*)v + (v·∇*)w lie in W_{α+μ−1/2}. For two curl-generated waves with the same label, the nonzero harmonics of the symmetric product lie in W_{α+α′−κs} and the zero harmonic lies in M_{α+α′−κs}. Distinct labels give zero products.

coverage.why: mispaired: the Lean statement bounds a curl remainder of a curl-generated coefficient, giving exponent α+1/2−κ. The paper's Lemma 9.2 bounds mean–wave and wave–wave transport products, with exponents α+μ−1/2 and α+α′−κs. The candidate-manuscript numbering likely differs.
